newsitem.title: FRANCE: Russian-European group gets satellite launch deal.
newsitem.headline: Russian-European group gets satellite launch deal.

text.p: The Russian-European launch consortium Starsem said on Thursday it had won its first firm contract to launch 12 satellites for the Globalstar satellite telecoms network.
The Globalstar network is composed of 56 satellites each weighing about 500 kg built by the U.S. company Space Systems/Loral.

"The launches are scheduled for the end of 1998 aboard three SOYUZ-ICARE rockets from the Baikonour cosmodrome in Kazakhstan," the company said in a statement issued from its European headquarters near Paris.
It said the contract was signed on December 3. Financial terms were not disclosed.
The Starsem consortium was created in August of this year and enables European firms to enter the expanding market for the launch of satellites for mobile communications.
Russian shareholders own a 50 percent stake of the company, with shares equally divided between the Russian Space Agency (RKA) and the Samara Space Center.
France's Aerospatiale owns 35 percent and the Arianespace satellite launch company 15 percent.

"These services are aimed at the market for...and launches into low orbit, which complements the services offered by Arianespace... the performance characteristics of the Soyuz launch system means that it does not compete with, but rather complements Ariane," Arianespace said in a company publication.
